title: Strict quotient normalization of pullback completion
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a morphism $g:U\to X$ of schemes. Use the completed coefficient sheaves $B_W$ and their positive quotient projections [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $g^*$ and $j_!$ denote the ordinary exact completed-coefficient pullback and, for open $j$, extension by zero and their termwise complex functors [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data]. Use the actual quotient completion $C_W$, its augmentation unit $\eta_W$, the strict quotient towers, flat-term K-flat representatives, and completed pullback $F_g$ of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. A normalized pull-completion presentation is a record consisting of preservation of the good representative class by ordinary pullback; an isomorphism of entire strict complex towers $\operatorname{red}_U(g^*P)\simeq (g^*(P_n))_n$, sending the quotient generator of the ordinary pullback unit to the finite pullback unit applied to $1\otimes x$; and a natural isomorphism $C_U\circ g^*\simeq F_g$. On every good representative, the latter followed by the defining $F_g$ representative comparison equals $C_U$ of the ordinary exact localization comparison, followed by the defining $C_U$ representative comparison and the functorial Roos map of the preceding strict-tower isomorphism. The record also retains the conversion from the global branch of the slice good predicate to the integral good predicate. Define the ordinary-to-completed map as $g^*\eta_U$ followed by this normalized comparison. All operation functors, quotient units and transition maps are the recorded ones.
